variants.text: Byron Bay is a beachside town of 6,330 people (2021 census) in the far north-east corner of New South Wales, 772 km north of Sydney and 165 km south of Brisbane. Cape Byron, the headland beside it, is the easternmost point of mainland Australia. People come for the surf beaches, diving at Julian Rocks, whale watching and a wellness and alternative scene, around 2 million of them a year (2018 figure). The traditional name for the place is Cavvanbah, 'meeting place'.
variants.claims: population, distances, easternmost, visitor figure, attractions, Cavvanbah: WP, WV, VNSW (what_and_where.fact)

variants.text: Byron Bay sits in Bundjalung Country, where Cook named the cape in 1770 and the traditional name Cavvanbah means 'meeting place'. Today it is a town of 6,330 people (2021 census) that draws around 2 million visitors a year (2018 figure), 772 km north of Sydney and 165 km south of Brisbane. Surf beaches and reef diving at Julian Rocks sit alongside a wellness and alternative scene. The hinterland has its own stops, among them Crystal Castle and Shambhala Gardens and the village of Bangalow.
variants.claims: Bundjalung Country, Cook 1770, Cavvanbah, figures, distances: WP/WV (what_and_where.fact); hinterland Crystal Castle and Bangalow: VNSW (whyVisit_note)

variants.text: The town of Byron Bay (6,330 people at the 2021 census) lies in the far north-east of New South Wales, 165 km south of Brisbane, with Cape Byron and its lighthouse on the headland beside it. Surfers, divers and whale watchers share the coast, and Julian Rocks, about 2.5 km offshore, is a marine park dive site where temperate and tropical waters merge. Around 2 million people visit each year (2018 figure). Inland, the hills behind the town hold Mullumbimby, Bangalow and Crystal Castle.
variants.claims: population/distance/figure: WP, WV; Julian Rocks 2.5 km, merge of waters: WP, WV; hinterland names: VNSW + placement.json

tips.text: Parking at the lighthouse is paid and capped at one hour per vehicle per day (about $10 an hour at the time of writing), so most people walk up from town along the beach, which takes about 20 minutes.
tips.source: NPWS-L, NPWS-W (fees as fetched 2026, may change); WV for the 20 min walk

tips.text: Ewingsdale Road into town is slow in school holidays and summer; Wikivoyage suggests leaving the M1 at the Lennox Head exit (Ross Lane) and coming in from the south. There is no train, and the nearest airports are Ballina/Byron (about 30 minutes) and Gold Coast (about an hour).
Main Beach is patrolled all summer, but Wategos and other beaches only over the Christmas school holidays, so swim at Main Beach outside that. Winter days reach only about 20 C.
Late November to early December is Schoolies week, which Wikivoyage suggests may be a time to avoid, and Easter brings the Bluesfest crowds.
Main Beach is the one patrolled all summer; Wategos is patrolled only over the Christmas school holidays.

The lighthouse carpark is limited at weekends and charges per hour with a one-hour daily maximum, so the 3.7 km Walgun walking track from town is the easier way up; the park can close for weather or fire danger.

bestMonths.note: Editorial inference; no source lists best months. September is the driest month (47 mm), Oct-Nov about 95 mm (WP climate); May is the editor's lesser pick, April is the wettest month (183.5 mm), so April is dropped. Whales best Sept-Oct (WV), peak Jul-Sep (VNSW).
